title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Answers to Several Questions Concerning the Application of the Foreign Economic Contract Law
keywords_en: sales contract; lease contract; contract for work; transport contract; insurance contract; guarantee
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice of Issuing the "Answers to Certain Questions Concerning the Application of the Law on Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests"

Fa (Jing) Fa [1987] No. 27

All local people's courts at various levels, all military courts, all railway transport intermediate courts and basic courts, and all maritime courts:

The "Answers to Certain Questions Concerning the Application of the Law on Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests" are hereby issued to you for implementation and enforcement in the trial of foreign-related economic cases. Any problems or comments arising during implementation shall be promptly reported to this Court.

October 19, 1987

Supreme People's Court

Answers to Certain Questions Concerning the Application of the Law on Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests

1. Scope of Application of the Law on Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests

(1) The scope of application of the Law on Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests is economic contracts concluded between enterprises or other economic organizations within China and foreign enterprises, other economic organizations, or individuals, including contracts for the sale of goods, contracts for equity joint ventures, contracts for contractual joint ventures, contracts for cooperative exploration and development of natural resources, loan contracts, lease contracts, technology transfer contracts, project contracting contracts, contracts for the supply of complete sets of equipment, processing and assembling contracts, labor service contracts, compensation trade contracts, contracts for scientific and technological consulting or design, guarantee contracts, insurance contracts, warehousing and storage contracts, and agency contracts. However, international maritime transport contracts, international air transport contracts, international railway transport contracts, and international multimodal transport contracts are excluded.

(2) The Law on Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests may also apply to the above-mentioned economic contracts concluded between enterprises, other economic organizations, or individuals in the Hong Kong and Macao regions and enterprises or other economic organizations in mainland China, as well as to the above-mentioned economic contracts concluded or performed within the territory of China between foreign enterprises, other economic organizations, or individuals, between enterprises, other economic organizations, or individuals in the Hong Kong and Macao regions, or between foreign enterprises, other economic organizations, or individuals and enterprises, other economic organizations, or individuals in the Hong Kong and Macao regions.

(3) Economic contracts concluded between Chinese-foreign equity joint ventures, Chinese-foreign contractual joint ventures, and wholly foreign-owned enterprises established within the territory of China, and between such enterprises and other enterprises, economic organizations, or individuals in China, shall not be governed by the Law on Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests but shall be governed by the Economic Contract Law of the People's Republic of China.

2. Application of Law to Disputes over Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests

(1) The term "contract disputes" as used in Article 5 of the Law on Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests shall be construed broadly. It shall include all disputes between the parties concerning whether a contract is formed, the time of formation, the interpretation of contract terms, performance of the contract, liability for breach, and the modification, suspension, assignment, rescission, or termination of the contract.

(2) Where the parties have chosen the law applicable to the contract at the time of its conclusion or after a dispute arises, the people's court shall take the law chosen by the parties as the basis when hearing the contract dispute case. The law chosen by the parties may be Chinese law, the law of the Hong Kong or Macao region, or foreign law. However, the parties' choice must be made through mutual consultation and must be express.

(3) For contracts for Chinese-foreign equity joint ventures, Chinese-foreign contractual joint ventures, and Chinese-foreign cooperative exploration and development of natural resources that are performed within the territory of China, Chinese law must be applied. Any contract clause by which the parties agree to choose foreign law shall be void.

(4) Where the parties have not chosen the law applicable to the contract at the time of its conclusion or after a dispute arises, the people's court, after accepting the case, shall allow the parties to make a choice before the trial hearing. If the parties still cannot reach an agreement on the choice, the people's court shall determine the applicable law in accordance with the principle of the closest connection.

(5) The law applicable to the resolution of contract disputes chosen by the parties through agreement or determined by the people's court in accordance with the principle of the closest connection refers to the current substantive law, and does not include conflict-of-laws rules or procedural rules.

(6) If the parties have not chosen the law applicable to the contract, the people's court shall, in accordance with the principle of the closest connection, determine the law to be applied to the following types of economic contracts involving foreign interests, which under normal circumstances shall be:

1. For international sales of goods contracts, the law of the place where the seller has its place of business at the time of the conclusion of the contract. However, if the contract was negotiated and concluded at the place where the buyer has its place of business, or if the contract was mainly concluded on the terms determined by the buyer and in response to a tender issued by the buyer, or if the contract explicitly provides that the seller must perform its delivery obligation at the place where the buyer has its place of business, then the law of the place where the buyer has its place of business at the time of the conclusion of the contract shall apply.

2. For bank loan or guarantee contracts, the law of the place where the lending bank or the guaranteeing bank is located.

3. For insurance contracts, the law of the place where the insurer has its place of business.

4. For processing and assembling contracts, the law of the place where the processor or assembler has its place of business.

5. For technology transfer contracts, the law of the place where the transferee has its place of business.

6. For project contracting contracts, the law of the place where the project is located.

7. For contracts for scientific and technological consulting or design, the law of the place where the client has its place of business.

8. For labor service contracts, the law of the place where the labor service is performed.

9. For contracts for the supply of complete sets of equipment, the law of the place where the equipment is installed and operated.

10. For agency contracts, the law of the place where the agent has its place of business.

11. For contracts for the lease, sale, or mortgage of immovable property, the law of the place where the immovable property is located.

12. For contracts for the lease of movable property, the law of the place where the lessor has its place of business.

13. For warehousing and storage contracts, the law of the place where the warehouseman or storage operator has its place of business.

However, if the contract is manifestly more closely connected with the law of another country or region, the people's court shall take the law of that other country or region as the basis for resolving the contract dispute.

(7) If a party has more than one place of business, the place of business that has the closest connection with the contract shall prevail. If a party has no place of business, its domicile or habitual residence shall prevail.

(8) If an international treaty concluded or acceded to by China contains provisions different from those of the Law on Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests or other Chinese laws relating to economic contracts involving foreign interests, the provisions of the international treaty shall prevail, except for the provisions on which China has made reservations.

(9) Where Chinese law is to be applied, but Chinese law has no provisions on the issues in dispute between the parties to the contract, international practices may be applied.

(10) Where the law to be applied is foreign law, if the application of such foreign law would violate the fundamental principles of Chinese law or the public interest of Chinese society, it shall not be applied, and the corresponding Chinese law shall be applied instead.

(11) Where the law to be applied is foreign law, and the people's court is unable to ascertain its content, the content may be ascertained through the following channels:

1. Provided by the parties;

2. Provided by the Chinese embassy or consulate in that country;

3. Provided by the embassy or consulate of that country in China;

4. Provided by Chinese or foreign legal experts.

If the content still cannot be ascertained through the above channels, the matter may be handled by reference to the corresponding Chinese law.

3. Confirmation of Invalidity of Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests

An economic contract involving foreign interests shall be confirmed as invalid in any of the following circumstances:

1. The party concluding the contract does not have legal subject status;

2. The Chinese party concluding the contract has not been granted foreign business operation rights upon approval by the competent state authority;

3. The Chinese party concluding the contract exceeds the scope of its business operations;

4. The contract is concluded in the name of a principal without power of agency, beyond the scope of agency authority, or after the termination of agency authority, and has not been ratified by the principal, unless the principal, upon learning of the above circumstances, fails to make a timely disclaim;

5. The contract is not concluded in writing;

6. For a contract that is required by Chinese laws or administrative regulations to be established upon approval by a competent state authority, approval has not been obtained, or a material modification or assignment of rights and obligations has not been approved by the original approving authority;

7. One party intentionally fabricates falsehoods, conceals the truth, or uses other deceptive means to cause the other party to enter into the contract under a mistaken impression; or uses coercive means, threatening to cause economic loss or other harm to the other party, to force the other party into the contract; or takes advantage of the other party's distress to force the other party to enter into the contract on unfair terms against its own will;

8. The parties maliciously collude to conclude a contract that harms the interests of the state, a collective, or a third party, or conclude a contract in a lawful form to conceal an unlawful purpose;

9. The content of the contract violates the fundamental principles of Chinese law or the public interest of Chinese society.

4. Rescission of Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests

A party shall have the right to request the people's court to rescind an economic contract involving foreign interests in any of the following circumstances:

(1) The contract was concluded due to a material misunderstanding concerning the content of the contract;

(2) The contract is manifestly unfair.

A rescinded economic contract involving foreign interests shall have no legal binding force from the time of its conclusion.

5. Consequences of Confirmation of Invalidity or Rescission of Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests

(1) If some clauses of a contract are invalid, but the invalidity does not affect the validity of the remaining clauses, the remaining clauses shall remain valid. If the invalid clauses are cancelled or corrected by agreement between the parties, the validity of the contract shall not be affected.

(2) If a contract is confirmed as invalid or rescinded due to the fault of one party, the party at fault shall be liable for compensating the other party for the losses suffered as a result of the invalidity or rescission. If both parties are at fault, each shall bear its corresponding liability.

(3) Where the parties maliciously collude, purporting to conclude an economic contract involving foreign interests to carry out activities that violate state laws or harm the public interest, or to harm the interests of the state or a third party, in addition to confirming the invalidity of the contract, any property illegally obtained by the parties shall be confiscated and turned over to the state or returned to the third party. Depending on the seriousness of the circumstances, sanctions such as reprimand, fine, or detention may be imposed in accordance with the law. If economic crimes are discovered, the case shall be transferred to the public security or prosecutorial authorities for investigation.

6. Liability for Breach of Economic Contracts Involving Foreign Interests

(1) If one party fails to perform the contract or performs its contractual obligations not in conformity with the agreed conditions, unless other remedial measures are taken or otherwise provided for in the contract, the breaching party shall compensate the other party for the losses suffered as a result. Such compensation shall generally include damage to or destruction, diminution, or loss of property, expenses incurred to reduce or eliminate the loss, and the profits that could have been obtained if the contract had been performed (in the case of international sales of goods contracts, this refers to profits). However, such compensation shall not exceed the loss that the breaching party should have foreseen at the time of concluding the contract as a possible consequence of the breach.

(2) The liquidated damages stipulated in the contract by the parties are predetermined compensation. If one party breaches the contract, it shall pay the stipulated liquidated damages to the other party. If the stipulated liquidated damages are substantially higher or lower than the loss caused by the breach, the people's court may, at the request of the party, appropriately reduce or increase them at its discretion.
